execution.description: The owner's two answers of 2026-10-03, built. Carbon's agent carries the last 3 messages it read into a new epoch (RSURF-D14). The Tools tab became a working toolbox over the agent's own research tools (RSURF-D15 to D18).

expected: A miner can use every research tool from the page with exactly the gates, limits and refusals an MCP agent gets, without a second ownership model, and a new epoch keeps the miner's guidance.
observed: The cleanest way to keep the two doors from drifting was to make the page call the same objects. The page's tools are the Tool instances standard_server._create_server builds, called through Tool.run, so schemas, validation and refusal text are equal by construction, and a test compares them tool by tool with the MCP server's. The ownership lock already serialised attach, practice, freeze and submit, so the page takes it the way carbon_attach_campaign does and says who can hold it when it cannot. Three limits surfaced only by trying. A workspace action's arguments are bounded at 16 KiB, below the tool's 32 KiB, so write_file takes about 11 KiB of file at a time. The page's CSP blocked data: images; blob: images made from checked raster bytes fit it with the smallest change. And the unchanged carrier keeps stdout only for a successful run and never keeps stderr, so the page says so and suggests sys.stderr = sys.stdout. Carrying messages forward needed only a v2 rule, an optional carried list in the epoch's first record, and the chain link binding it, so v1 records and links are untouched.
keep: Give a second door the first door's own objects (the Tool instances), not a reimplementation, and test the two against each other per tool.
Reuse the existing ownership lock as the session model, and say plainly who can hold it and what to do.
Version a frozen rule (v1 to v2) instead of reinterpreting it, and bind new record fields into the chain only when they are present.
Build the demo's session from the real tools over an SDK that has nothing to dispatch with.
change: Check a tool's nested argument bounds, not only its outer bound, before sizing an editor.
Check the page's CSP before rendering a new kind of content; prefer blob: over data:.
Ask the owner whether the carrier should keep stderr and a failed run's stdout: today a failing program shows only its failure code.
protocol_elements: the Control Center is one more client of the research tools, under the campaign's ownership lock
a run's own output is one shared read-only operation, bounded, text and raster images only
